item.title: ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde
item.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. That was what produced the boy, and I was finally left off the hook,” he said. Vanguard News The post ‘I bought a book on how to have a boy-child’ – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people . The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away. The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability. The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars. Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared. “We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster. “Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. item.title: Why Niniola and I have never released a song together – Teni
item.description: Nigerian singer Teni has explained why she and her elder sister, fellow music star Niniola, have yet to release a song together despite their individual successes in the music industry. The singer made the revelation during a question and answer session on Tea with Taylor , hosted by actor Taymesan Emmanuel. Comedian Bovi, who was among the audience, asked Teni why the sisters had never collaborated on a song, prompting her to explain that their conversations rarely revolve around music. According to her, whenever they meet or speak, they spend most of their time chatting and discussing other matters rather than working on music. “We are just two crazy girls. We will just be doing amebo and gisting all the time, forgetting to make music,” she said. She added that music hardly comes up whenever they speak, but suggested that fans could finally get the long-awaited collaboration in 2027. “I kid you not, every time Nini and I talk, we never talk about music. I know it’s bad. We are going to give you guys come 2027,” Teni said. The singer’s comments have renewed anticipation among fans for a joint project from the sisters, whose careers have developed independently within the Nigerian music industry. Teni, whose full name is Teniola Apata, gained prominence with songs such as Uyo Meyo and Case , while Niniola, born Niniola Apata, established herself with popular tracks including Maradona and Bana . Both singers have earned recognition for their distinct musical styles, with Teni known for her playful delivery and Niniola celebrated for her blend of Afro-house and other contemporary African sounds. Although they have not released a joint song, Teni’s latest remarks suggest that a collaboration could be on the way in 2027. item.title: Anambra: Pregnant woman delivers after APLUC seals building
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — A nine-month pregnant woman, Mrs Nkechi Theophlus, has delivered her baby after reportedly collapsing following the sealing of her residential building by officials of the Anambra State Property and Land Use Charge (APLUC) in Obosi, Idemili North Local Government Area of the state. The woman reportedly went into labour and delivered her baby in the early hours of Thursday after being rushed to a hospital following the incident. The incident occurred at No. 1 Anyeji Omenwa Street, Obosi, where the officials allegedly padlocked the main entrance to the compound and sealed the building with red tape. The sealing reportedly left the landlady, Prophetess Ukamaka Lauretta Okafor, tenants and other occupants of the three-storey building, comprising 11 flats and rooms in the boys’ quarters, unable to gain access to their homes. The landlady, who protested the action, accused APLUC officials of refusing to issue her a receipt for the N120,000 she allegedly paid to the agency in February, while demanding additional payments. Addressing journalists on Thursday, Okafor said she was not indebted to the agency, insisting that the officials had failed to provide evidence of the full payment she made. She alleged that although N120,000 was deducted from her account through the officials’ Point of Sale (POS) machine, she was issued a receipt for only N90,000. According to her, the officials promised to provide a receipt for the outstanding N30,000 at their office but failed to do so despite her repeated visits. She said she was subsequently informed that the N120,000 payment covered her 2024 liability, while further payments were required for 2025 and 2026. Okafor said she expressed willingness to settle the outstanding payments but insisted that she must first receive evidence of the previous payment. She alleged that the officials refused to issue receipts or a covering note for subsequent payments, instead asking her to pay cash or surrender her ATM card for transactions through their POS machine. She said: “As I am speaking with you now, the N120,000 I paid in February this year, they have not given me the receipt. “I now told them that I will not continue to pay money that won’t be receipted or any evidence of payment given to me. I even told them to give me a covering note for me to pay all the money they are demanding, that I am ready at any moment to pay all the money they are demanding, but they insisted they won’t give me any receipt or covering note.” The landlady also alleged that the enforcement exercise was carried out without prior notice to her or other occupants of the building. She said the sealing left children returning from school and other tenants stranded outside their homes, with some forced to spend the night outdoors. item.title: Full list as CAF shortlist 5 for Women’s Player of the Year award
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled five finalists for the 2026 Women’s Player of the Year award, with Malawi sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga leading a shortlist featuring some of the continent’s outstanding footballers. Cameroon’s Monique Ngock, Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Morocco’s Hanane Aït El Haj complete the five-player list for African women’s football’s highest individual honour. The finalists were selected from an initial shortlist of 10 nominees based on their performances for club and country during the year. The shortlist reflects an eventful year for women’s football in Africa, highlighted by Cameroon’s historic triumph at the TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) Morocco 2026 and Malawi’s remarkable run to the final on their tournament debut. The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards 2026 in Lagos, Nigeria, on Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre. The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. 5 finalists for CAF Women’s Player of the Year 2026 1. Monique Ngock (Cameroon / Washington Spirit) Cameroon’s Monique Ngock earned a place among the finalists following her influential performances in helping the Indomitable Lionesses win their first WAFCON title at the 2026 tournament in Morocco. The midfielder was named Best Player of the Tournament after playing a key role in Cameroon’s historic campaign, which ended with a 3-0 victory over Malawi in the final in Rabat. Her commanding displays, technical ability and leadership in midfield also earned her a place in CAF’s official Team of the Tournament. Her contributions to the national team, alongside her performances for US club Washington Spirit, have strengthened her reputation as one of Africa’s leading midfielders. 2. Temwa Chawinga (Malawi / Kansas City Current) Temwa Chawinga enjoyed an outstanding year, helping Malawi reach the WAFCON 2026 final on their tournament debut and secure historic qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The forward won the Golden Boot at the tournament after scoring five goals and providing two assists. She finished level on goals with Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Cameroon’s Marie Ngah Manga but claimed the award on the strength of her assists. Temwa’s performances also earned her a place in CAF’s Team of the Tournament. 3. Tabitha Chawinga (Malawi / OL Lyonnes) Tabitha Chawinga joins her younger sister Temwa on the final shortlist after playing an important role in Malawi’s impressive campaign at WAFCON 2026. item.title: Ebonyi NDC deputy gov candidate defects to APC; declares support for Tinubu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Ambassador Uka Chris Ndubuisi, has defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC), declaring support for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Francis Nwifuru. Ndubuisi announced his decision at the APC governorship campaign rally in Ebonyi State on Thursday, saying he had chosen to leave the NDC and collapse the party’s structure in the state. “My name is Ambassador Uka Chris Ndubuisi, and I am the Deputy Governorship candidate of NDC, and also the NDC Youth National Publicity Secretary. “No two ways. I just want to make this declaration that I have decided. Nobody forced me to it; on my own, I have decided to give my support to Mr President Bola Tinubu and our beloved Governor, His Excellency Francis Nwifuru. From today, we are collapsing the structure of NDC in Ebonyi State,” he said. Ndubuisi was received by Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Former governor and Minister of Works, David Umahi and APC supporters in the state. Umahi presented him to the party chairman, who was to formally hand him over to Nwifuru, the party’s leader in the state. According to INEC, Ndubuisi was listed as the running mate to NDC governorship candidate Senator Paulinus Igwe Nwagu for the February 6, 2027 election. The ticket was set to challenge incumbent Governor Francis Nwifuru and his deputy, Patricia Obila, who are seeking re-election on the APC platform. item.title: Nobody will love us the way Tinubu loves us in Ebonyi — Gov Nwifuru
item.description: Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has urged residents to vote for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying the president has demonstrated love for the state through projects and deserves overwhelming support in return. Nwifuru said Ebonyi residents should repay Tinubu’s gesture by delivering 100 per cent of their votes to him in the next presidential election. The governor spoke on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress governorship campaign, where he said he was more concerned about mobilising support for Tinubu than campaigning for himself. “The president has given us a project that nobody ever envisaged we will have, and to pay back is to vote for Mr President 100 per cent,” he said. Nwifuru said the state’s political leadership had promised Tinubu 1.3 million votes, expressing confidence that residents would fulfil the pledge. “Our leader said we are promising him 1.3 million votes. I want to tell you, I’m not here to campaign for myself. I am here to campaign for our dear president,” the governor said. He urged the people to acknowledge the projects and interventions the president had brought to Ebonyi, saying the benefits were visible and should not be overlooked. According to him, the Minister of Works had already outlined the projects executed or being undertaken in the state, adding that residents should take the message to their communities. Nwifuru insisted that Tinubu’s commitment to Ebonyi was unmatched, urging residents to demonstrate their appreciation through their votes. “You refused to see what he’s done, and it’s something that is very practical. The Honourable Minister of Works has enumerated it, you’ve heard from him, but I want you to take this message home,” he said. “No other person will love us the way President Bola Ahmed Tinubu loves us, and it’s a payback time,” the governor added. item.title: 74 Killed In Niger Communal Clash, Bago Orders Investigation, Donates N148m To Families
item.description: The clash between Kambari vigilantes and Fulani herders in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State resulted in the death of 74 persons. The state’s governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, disclosed this during a visit to the Emir of Borgu, Alhaji Halilu Sani Dantoro, at his palace in New Bussa, the LGA’s headquarters. Terrorists had, last Saturday, attacked Lumman-Ba’are community in Borgu LGA, killing the village head, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, his wife and three of his children. They also set his palace ablaze. Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, has ordered a thorough investigation into the clashes.‎ ‎The governor commiserated with the traditional ruler and people of the kingdom over the tragic incident. ‎Bago said the investigation was aimed at identifying those responsible for the violence and uncovering the remote and immediate causes of the recurring communal conflicts, with a view to preventing future occurrences. ‎He called on residents of the affected communities to embrace peaceful coexistence, tolerance and mutual understanding, stressing that no meaningful development could take place in an atmosphere of violence and hostility. ‎The governor expressed sympathy with the families of the victims and announced a donation of ₦2 million to each of the 74 affected families, amounting to ₦148 million, alongside the provision of foodstuffs and building materials to support those whose houses were destroyed during the clashes. ‎He commended the Borgu Emirate Council for its continued efforts towards maintaining peace and unity among the people, while urging Nigerians to learn to live together irrespective of their differences. ‎In his response, the Emir of Borgu, Muhammad Haliru -Dantoro Kitoro IV, appreciated the governor for the condolence visit and the timely deployment of security personnel to the area. ‎The traditional ruler acknowledged the state government’s efforts in deploying joint tactical security teams to tackle security challenges, including insurgency, in the area. He, however, expressed sadness that some individuals had chosen to resort to violence despite ongoing efforts by the government and security agencies to restore lasting peace. ‎The Emir also commended security agencies for their swift response, which he said helped to contain the situation and restore normalcy to the affected communities. ‎In his remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi, commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his efforts towards addressing security challenges across the country, noting that the restructuring of the nation’s security architecture was yielding positive results. ‎He also praised Governor Bago for his commitment to tackling insecurity in parts of Niger State and acknowledged the contributions of security agencies in containing threats to lives and property. ‎The governor was accompanied on the visit by the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi; Member representing Borgu/Agwara Federal Cons

item.title: FG issues strong advisory on harmattan fires, flags off safety campaign
item.description: …Warns against attacks on firefighters, careless fuel storage By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has issued a strong advisory on the risk of fire during the harmattan season, urging Nigerians to avoid overloading electrical sockets, leaving cooking unattended, burning refuse indiscriminately and storing petrol carelessly. The Controller General of the Federal Fire Service FFS, Samuel Adeyemi Olumode, gave the advisory on Thursday while flagging off the 2026 Harmattan Fire Safety Campaign. The campaign will run through February 2027. He spoke via a virtual fire chat on “The Roles and Responsibilities of Stakeholders in Building a Fire Safety-Resilient Community.” “The Harmattan period comes with dry and dusty weather conditions, low humidity and dry vegetation, all of which can contribute to the rapid spread of fire. “Activities involving cooking, electrical appliances, generators, gas cylinders, fuel storage and open burning require greater caution during this period”, he said. He advised households to “regularly inspect gas cylinders, hoses and connections, and ensure that generators are operated in properly ventilated outdoor spaces.” Parents and guardians, he said, “must also keep matches, lighters and other ignition sources away from children.” Olumode also warned business owners, market operators, school administrators, event organisers and managers of public facilities to put proper fire safety arrangements in place. “Prevention should never be treated as an expense that can be postponed until an emergency occurs,” he said. The Controller General condemned a recent attack on firefighters who were attacked at 7th Avenue, Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Friday, 13th November 2026. “At about 10am, firefighters from the Kubwa Metropolitan Fire Station, who had responded to a distress call, were attacked by suspected hoodlums who pelted them with stones. One of our personnel sustained a head injury and required medical attention. “Let me state clearly that attacks on firefighters will not be tolerated,” Olumode declared, adding that the suspected perpetrators had been apprehended. “Let me assure Nigerians that this matter will not be treated lightly. The appropriate authorities will ensure that those found culpable face the full weight of the law. There must be no justification for violence against emergency responders”, he said. The CGF said no emergency response system could function effectively “when firefighters are attacked, obstructed or prevented from carrying out their duties.” Olumode linked the safety of responders to the Service’s 15-minute response-time target. item.title: WhatsApp to allow users schedule messages – here’s how you can
item.description: WhatsApp has introduced a scheduled messaging feature that allows users to compose messages in advance and choose when they should be delivered, addressing one of the most requested additions to the messaging platform. The feature will enable users to schedule messages between 10 minutes and 14 days ahead in both individual and group chats. Announcing the update, WhatsApp said the feature would allow users to write messages when they think of them and have them delivered at a more appropriate time. “That’s why we’re introducing scheduled messages – one of our most requested features. You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats,” the company said. According to WhatsApp, scheduled messages will appear in recipients’ chats like ordinary messages, without any indication that they were composed and scheduled earlier. Users will also be able to view all their scheduled messages and delete them before delivery if they change their minds. How to schedule messages on WhatsApp To schedule a message on WhatsApp, users can follow these steps: Open WhatsApp and select an individual or group chat. Type the message they want to send. Press and hold the send button. Select the preferred date and time for the message to be delivered. Confirm the schedule. The message will then be delivered automatically at the selected time. WhatsApp said scheduled messages would still be delivered even if the sender’s phone was switched off or ran out of battery. The feature will support text messages, photographs and videos, giving users the option to plan different types of communication ahead of time. The company also assured users that scheduled messages would retain WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption, meaning only the sender and intended recipients would be able to read them. “Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us,” WhatsApp said. The scheduled messaging feature is rolling out globally over the coming weeks, although the company did not specify when it would become available to all users. WhatsApp said the update was another way for users to stay connected with important people by ensuring their messages arrive at exactly the right time. item.title: Nigeria’s trade hits ₦41.4tn in Q2 as NPA records 24.8% cargo growth
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s expanding trade activities are increasingly highlighting the strategic importance of the maritime sector, with cargo volumes handled across the nation’s seaports recording significant growth amid rising merchandise trade. The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) disclosed that cargo throughput across Nigerian ports rose by 24.8 per cent, from 103.6 million metric tonnes in 2024 to 129.3 million metric tonnes in 2025, indicating increased port utilisation and growing cargo-handling activities. The growth momentum extended into the first half of 2026, as cargo throughput increased by 12.2 per cent to 68.2 million metric tonnes, compared with 60.8 million metric tonnes recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The development comes against the backdrop of Nigeria’s merchandise trade rising to ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, further highlighting the critical role of ports in facilitating international trade, cargo movement and broader economic activities. Speaking at a two-day data-driven business and maritime reporting training organised in partnership with the Premium Times Training Academy in Ikeja, Lagos, on Wednesday, the General Manager, Corporate Affairs Division, NPA, Mr Ikechukwu Onyemekara, urged journalists to embrace evidence-based journalism, saying accurate maritime reporting was critical to trade, investment decisions and public understanding of the economy. He said Nigeria’s merchandise trade value of ₦41.4 trillion in the second quarter of 2026, representing a 5.6 per cent increase over the corresponding period of 2025, demonstrated the scale of economic activity linked to the movement of cargo through the country’s ports. According to him, port efficiency has far-reaching implications for manufacturers, exporters, importers, consumers and investors, as delays and operational bottlenecks ultimately increase the cost of doing business and affect the prices of goods. Onyemekara said the country’s ports received 2,300 ships in the first half of 2026, compared with 2,152 vessels in the same period of 2025, while outward cargo accounted for 41.9 per cent of total throughput in the second quarter, indicating improved export activity. He urged maritime journalists to look beyond headline figures and examine the factors driving growth, citing Lekki Deep Sea Port, which handled nearly 40 per cent of cargo throughput across Nigerian ports in the first half of 2026. He said more than three-quarters of Lekki’s cargo traffic was linked to refinery operations, stressing that a breakdown of the figures was necessary to understand how industrial investments were reshaping port activities and trade flows. On the NPA’s reform efforts, Onyemekara said the authority was pursuing port modernisation, digitalisation, export facilitation and sustainability initiatives to improve efficiency and competitiveness. item.title: Plateau Attack: Death toll rises to 19
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The death toll from an attack on Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), a community in Jebbu Miango, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, has risen to 19 following the death of three persons who were rushed to hospital after the incident. The attack reportedly occurred on Wednesday night, November 25, and continued into the early hours of Thursday, November 26, 2026, throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. A resident of the community, Moses Monday, who confirmed the casualty figure on Thursday, said 16 bodies were recovered at the scene, while three other victims died after being taken to hospital. Monday said: “This is evil. I can confirm that 16 bodies have so far been recovered at the spot, with an additional three who died after they were taken to the hospital. These evil men will not rest.” Another resident, Nuhu Fidelis, who also confirmed the attack, described it as another assault on a neighbouring community in Jebbu Miango. Fidelis said: “Yes, in the early morning of today, Thursday. Last night, November 25, 2026, a Christian neighbouring village, Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), in Jebbu Miango, Bassa LGA, Plateau State, was attacked again. Many innocent people lost their lives.” He condemned the killings and called on the government and security agencies to take urgent measures to protect residents. Another resident, Paul Nehemiah, who said he lost a close relative in the attack, described the killings as wicked and unprovoked, adding that residents had been living in fear following repeated attacks. Nehemiah said: “We are tired of burying our people. These are farmers, women and children who did nothing to anyone. How long will this continue? We are calling on the government to rise up and save us.” Rita Joseph, whose family fled the village during the attack, said community members could no longer sleep peacefully because of persistent security threats. She said: “We ran into the bush with our children.” The residents appealed to the Plateau State Government, the Federal Government and security agencies to deploy more personnel to Miango and surrounding communities to prevent further attacks. They also urged the authorities to take decisive action to bring the perpetrators to justice and restore confidence among residents. Efforts to obtain comments from the Plateau State Police Command spokesman, SP Alfred Alabo, and his counterpart at Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, were unsuccessful, as they had yet to respond to inquiries by our correspondent as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations
item.description: ‎Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, has received the report of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry established to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 artisanal miners while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger State Command. ‎The Governor received the report from the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, at the Government House, Minna, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to implementing its recommendations. ‎Governor Bago expressed appreciation to the Commission on behalf of the bereaved families, the Miners Association and the NSCDC, describing the report as an important document that would guide stakeholders in addressing the circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. ‎He commended Justice Muhammad and members of the Commission for their dedication, sacrifices and thoroughness throughout the investigation, assuring that the government would carefully consider the findings and recommendations. ‎The Governor also disclosed that a copy of the report would be forwarded to the Presidency for reference, underscoring the importance of the investigation and its outcome. ‎Earlier, the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, thanked the Governor for the confidence reposed in the panel and the opportunity to serve. ‎He explained that the Commission received nine memoranda, conducted public hearings and carried out inspection visits to two mining sites, two NSCDC offices and the General Hospital in Minna as part of its investigation. ‎Justice Muhammad said the evidence and facts gathered during the proceedings formed the basis of the Commission’s findings and recommendations. ‎He further explained that the report was presented in three volumes for ease of reference, with Volume One containing the findings, observations and recommendations; Volume Two containing the records of proceedings; and Volume Three comprising all exhibits tendered before the Commission. ‎In his remarks, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Nasiru Mu’azu, described the deaths of the 37 artisanal miners as a grave incident in the history of Niger State. ‎He commended Governor Bago for demonstrating commitment to the rule of law by establishing the Judicial Commission of Inquiry to investigate the incident and ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were thoroughly examined. ‎Mu’azu assured that the Ministry of Justice would carefully study the report and advise the government on appropriate actions and the next steps to be taken. ‎ ‎ The post Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu housing projects deliver over 26,000 units, 525,100 jobs, APC-PCC says
item.description: …As MOFI implements N1 trillion mortgage programme By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC said on Thursday thst the President Bola Tinubu administration has facilitated the financing and delivery of over 26,000 housing units and generated 525,100 real estate construction jobs nationwide in the past three years. Spokesperson of the council, Dele Alake, made the claim in a statement issued in Abuja. According to the statement, the Ministry of Finance Incorporated MOFI, through the MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), has provided more than N158 billion in mortgage financing to 2,269 homebuyers as of October 31, 2026. The statement said the fund financed properties valued at more than N279 billion, while 695 housing units have received offtake guarantees, “creating a ready market for private-sector property development”. It said 6,620 properties have been listed on the fund’s platform, with 21 financial institutions providing mortgage services across 28 states and all six geopolitical zones. MREIF, a N1 trillion housing finance programme sponsored by MOFI, commenced operations on March 17, 2025, to expand access to affordable mortgages and mobilise private investment in the housing sector. The statement said beneficiaries can access mortgage loans at an interest rate of 9.75 per cent per annum, with repayment periods of up to 20 years and a minimum equity contribution of 10 per cent. It added that the fund raised an initial N250 billion, made up of N150 billion in concessionary Federal Government funding and N100 billion in private commercial investment. “To enable more Nigerians to own homes, President Tinubu’s administration recognises that affordable mortgage loans, reasonably priced developer financing, and local production of building materials are crucial to reducing housing costs and expanding construction activities,” the statement said. On construction, the council said the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development is building 10,328 housing units at different stages of completion under the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. These include 2,744 units at the Renewed Hope City in Abuja, 2,000 in Kano and 2,084 in Lagos, while another 3,500 units are being developed under the Renewed Hope Estates Programme across 14 states. The Federal Housing Authority FHA, it said, is delivering 3,341 units, including 1,550 units for armed forces personnel in Jabi, Abuja. The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria FMBN accounts for another 11,294 housing units, comprising 9,076 units financed between 2024 and 2025 and 2,218 units delivered in the first quarter of 2026. According to the statement, the ministry’s housing projects are estimated to have generated 258,200 employment opportunities, while FMBN’s interventions have generated 226,900. item.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has confirmed a criminal cyberattack that exposed a limited amount of personal and business information, while files linked to its abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan were not accessed. According to Reuters, a person with direct knowledge of the incident said less than 0.1 per cent of FIFA’s total data was affected and no files from the FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed. “FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters. The football governing body condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data, calling it “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”. FIFA did not disclose when the attack took place, how many people or organisations were affected, or what business information was accessed. It also did not say whether any data had appeared online or where it may have been published. FIFA scrapped plans in July to sell private investors a stake in a new unit that would manage its events, including the World Cup. The proposal aimed to raise up to $4.2 billion by selling a 20 per cent stake. The post FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meet Nigeria’s Damilola Bolarinde, crowned Miss International Africa 2026
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian beauty queen Damilola Bolarinde has been crowned Miss International Africa 2026 after representing the country at the 64th edition of the Miss International pageant in Tokyo, Japan. The continental title was announced on Thursday, November 26, a day after the grand finale held on November 25, which featured 73 contestants from different countries. Bolarinde, popularly known as Queen Dammy, secured a place among the Top 20 contestants but did not advance to the Top 10. Her performance at the competition earned her the Miss International Africa title. The achievement adds to her growing profile in the Nigerian beauty pageant industry, having represented Lagos State at the 2025 Miss Universe Nigeria competition, where she emerged first runner-up behind Anambra State representative, Onyinyechi Basil. In April 2026, Bolarinde won the Face of Hope pageant, earning the right to represent Nigeria at the Miss International competition as Miss International Nigeria 2026. She defeated contestants representing Anambra and Rivers states, who finished as first and second runners-up, respectively, at the event held on April 19 at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos. Meanwhile, Elizaveta Kuznetsova of Moldova won the overall Miss International 2026 crown, becoming the first contestant from her country to claim the title. Brittany Feeney of the United Kingdom finished as first runner-up, while Laura Glozarová of the Czech Republic came third. Victoria Kosasieputri of Indonesia and Khánh Như Lê of Vietnam completed the Top Five, finishing fourth and fifth, respectively. Bolarinde’s continental recognition marks another milestone in her pageant career and adds Nigeria to the list of countries represented among the award recipients at the international competition. item.title: Opposition coalition confirms Monday summit, to adopt 3 key documents
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Coalition for Democracy has confirmed that the Second Summit of Nigeria’s opposition political parties will hold on Monday in Abuja, with participating parties expected to adopt three foundational documents. The coalition is a multiparty platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP). In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties, it said the decision was reached on Wednesday night at the seventh meeting of its Central Leadership Committee. The statement said the leaders reached the decision “following extensive deliberations on the state of the nation, the prevailing political environment and the earlier resolution to suspend campaign activities on day of the Summit”. The leaders, however, made it clear that the suspension does not end inter-party engagement. “The leaders agreed that the suspension of campaign activities does not preclude the continuation of consultations and engagements among opposition political parties on matters of common interest, including electoral integrity, democratic participation and institutional reform,” the statement said. The documents to be considered and adopted are the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme. They were developed by working groups made up of representatives of the constituent parties after the inaugural summit of August 31, 2026. According to the statement, “the documents set out proposed mechanisms for inter-party cooperation and a framework for addressing national governance challenges.” The coalition leaders also reaffirmed their commitment “to working collectively to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and protect the sanctity of the ballot across the country”. The coalition invited other opposition political parties to participate in the summit and “contribute to the ongoing consultations”. Three personalities will address the summit on the theme, “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition”. They are the Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, HRH Oba Oladipo Olaitan; Prof. Ango Abdullahi; and Chief S. N. Okeke. The statement said the summit is expected to bring together “national leaders of opposition political parties, elected representatives, former public officeholders, civil society leaders, representatives of the media, and observers from foreign diplomatic missions in Nigeria”. item.title: 19 years after, Olajumoke’s hostels for disabled students decay
item.description: — Invaded by bedbugs, broken doors, faulty drains — Students seek urgent intervention as AAUA VC promises action By Dayo Johnson AKURE — Nineteen years after former Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Senator Bode Olajumoke, donated two hostels for students with disabilities, the facilities have fallen into a state of disrepair, with residents appealing to the university authorities for urgent intervention. Olajumoke, who visited the male and female hostels he donated in February 2006, expressed dismay at their condition, describing the facilities as horrible and neglected. Conducted round the buildings by the hostel manager, Joseph Aladegbola, the former senator said the living conditions of the students were unacceptable and urged the university management to urgently rehabilitate the facilities. Olajumoke donated the hostels after discovering that the institution had no accommodation specifically designed for students with disabilities. The two buildings, alongside an office for the hostel manager, were commissioned by former Senate President, Senator Ken Nnamani, with the late Governor Olusegun Agagu as guest of honour. They were purpose-built to accommodate students with physical disabilities, with wide doors and toilets and bathrooms designed to allow wheelchair access. However, the hostel manager attributed the poor state of the facilities to inadequate funding, saying the hostels received maintenance funds at most twice a year, an allocation he described as insufficient to address their needs. After inspecting the buildings, Olajumoke visited the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Tomola Obamuyi, where he raised concerns about the level of deterioration. He warned that the unhygienic conditions could trigger disease outbreaks if urgent steps were not taken to address them. Olajumoke said the male hostel was in a worse condition, adding that both buildings had been invaded by bedbugs and required immediate fumigation. He called on stakeholders to work together to improve the living conditions of students with disabilities. One of the students lamented that the rooms, bathrooms, toilets and kitchen were all in a state of neglect. “The institution has neglected the hostels, the toilets are bad, doors and windows falling, all other facilities are in deplorable conditions,” the student said. The student appealed to the university authorities to restore the buildings to the condition they were in when Olajumoke donated them. Also speaking, a former hall chairman, Joseph Agada, urged the university management to prioritise the renovation of the hostels before the situation deteriorated further. Agada called for comprehensive repairs, including the replacement of damaged bathroom and toilet facilities, provision of new chairs and fumigation to tackle the bedbug infestation. “We need the complete renovation of the two hostels, new chairs, the fumigation of the hostels because of the invasion of bedbugs. item.title: 2027: Violence, Intimidation, Use Of Thugs May Discourage Voters, Amupitan Warns Political Parties
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has condemned violence associated with political campaigns, warning political parties and their supporters against actions capable of threatening peace and undermining the electoral process. Amupitan warned on Thursday as ‎ the Commission and security agencies meet to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 general election. ‎The INEC Chairman stressed the need for political actors to embrace issue-based campaigns, respect opposing views and conduct their political activities within the provisions of the law. Stressing that no political ambition is worth the blood of the citizens ‎He noted that political violence, intimidation and the use of thugs recently witnessed in some states during campaigns could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the democratic process. ‎ Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, and National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, at the meeting. ‎Prof Amupitan said that the commission is working closely with the office of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to identify flash points across the country. ‎He noted that election security remains a collective responsibility, requiring all relevant agencies to work together in addressing violence, intimidation and other activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections. Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu at the meeting ‎Amupitan further emphasised the need for security agencies to operate with professionalism, impartiality and respect for the rule of law, warning that no political interest should be allowed to compromise their constitutional responsibilities. ‎In attendance are the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, the Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, among others. ‎The Inspector-General of Police, in his welcoming address, emphasised the need for improved collaboration, intelligence sharing and coordinated security operations to address potential threats to the electoral process. Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, at the meeting. While giving an update on preparations for the upcoming general elections during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), on Wednesday, Amuipitan said that the Commission is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. According to him, INEC has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. item.title: Mourners Mark Hong Kong Fire Anniversary, Authorities Warn Against ‘Disorder’
item.description: A stream of mourners laid flowers Thursday at the site of a horrific fire that ripped through a Hong Kong apartment complex and killed 168 people a year ago, with authorities warning against “acts of disorder”. The world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 began on the afternoon of November 26, 2025 and raged for two days, gutting seven of Wang Fuk Court’s eight high-rise buildings that were home to some 4,600 people. Authorities in the Chinese territory — where Beijing has cracked down on dissent — appear wary of commemorations taking on a political tone and plan no official memorial. Police on Thursday kept a low profile as mourners laid hundreds of bouquets at a small park beneath the charred shells of the ruined buildings. They included former residents who stood on the same spot a year ago desperately waiting for news of their loved ones. “Families are torn apart, and people died,” said Koey Tam, a housewife and former resident in her 40s who lost her home, adding that they “can never be compensated with a new flat and a huge sum of money”. Smoke rises from apartments after a major fire swept through several blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential estate in Hong Kong’s Tai Po district on November 27, 2025. (Photo by DALE DE LA REY / AFP) The government was “a bit cold” to hold no official memorials, she added. “What can a memorial event possibly affect?” Grace Chan, 69, expressed her frustration at what she called people’s “self-censorship”, telling reporters that “at first, I thought they’d given us a large space” to pay respects to the victims. “Too many Hongkongers remain silent,” she said, as she left a single chrysanthemum at the site. Former resident Dorz Cheung told AFP that he still felt “very, very, very angry” about the government’s response to oversights exposed in the tragedy. “There are still so many emotions… anger, deep sadness, they’re all around.” ‘Seeking Accountability’ A mourner brings flowers to Wang Fu Court in Hong Kong on November 26, 2026, the site of a horrific fire that ripped through seven apartment blocks and killed 168 people a year before. (Photo by Peter PARKS / AFP) The blaze was Hong Kong’s worst disaster in more than seven decades, and a shock to the 7.5 million residents of one of Asia’s safest cities. The city’s number two official Eric Chan said the government will offer help to “lawful” memorial events, but warned against “acts of disorder”. The Chinese government’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office spoke this week against attempts to “cause chaos” under the guise of commemorations. According to media reports, some local journalists have faced internal pressure when covering the fire, including to shelve programmes originally scheduled to go on air. A government spokesperson told AFP that as long as it is “within the law”, there are “no restrictions on the freedom to comment and criticise government policies for media outlets”.
